newsitem.title: UK: Britain says huge Montserrat eruption possible.
newsitem.headline: Britain says huge Montserrat eruption possible.

text.p: Britain said on Monday the volcano on the Caribbean island of Montserrat had become more dangerous and plans for a voluntary partial evacuation of remaining residents had been put into operation.

The possibility of a "massive, cataclysmic-intensive eruption" from the Soufriere Hills volcano on the British colony could no longer be ruled out, International Development Minister George Foulkes was quoted as saying by Britain's Press Association news agency.

He said he had been told by experts at the Montserrat Volcano Observatory: "The consequences of such an event, if it did occur, would be extreme and anywhere on the island could be significantly threatened."

Foulkes said: "Over the past 24 hours the volcano has become much more dangerous. As a result we have agreed to this voluntary partial evacuation of anyone who wants to leave in the wake of this information."
He said urgent talks were under way with the island's governor, Frank Savage.
The evacuation plan would take effect immediately and people would be given the opportunity to leave at once, he added.
The volcano began spewing ash and rock in July 1995.
The Press Association said some 4,000 people were still on Montserrat -- down from the pre-volcano eruption population of 11,000 -- and most of them were now confined to the rugged north.
